title: In both
prompt: Show the customer ids that appear in both customers and orders, using INTERSECT. Replace the ___.
hints: INTERSECT keeps rows found in both.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT id FROM customers INTERSECT SELECT customer_id FROM orders;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id FROM customers EXCEPT SELECT customer_id FROM orders;
wrongSolutions.why: Keeps those in only the first

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id FROM customers UNION SELECT customer_id FROM orders;

title: Only in the first
prompt: Show customer ids that have never placed an order, using EXCEPT.
hints: EXCEPT removes rows found in the second result.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT id FROM customers EXCEPT SELECT customer_id FROM orders;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id FROM customers INTERSECT SELECT customer_id FROM orders;
SELECT customer_id FROM orders EXCEPT SELECT id FROM customers;

title: Order matters
prompt: Show product ids that sold but aren't in the products table, using EXCEPT. Usually there are none, but check anyway.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 99, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT product_id FROM order_items EXCEPT SELECT id FROM products;

SELECT product_id FROM order_items INTERSECT SELECT id FROM products;

title: Taken Maths and Science
prompt: Show student_ids who've enrolled in course 1 and also in course 3, using INTERSECT.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring'); UPDATE enrolments SET course_id = 1 WHERE id = 11; UPDATE enrolments SET course_id = 3 WHERE id = 12;

solutions: SELECT student_id FROM enrolments WHERE course_id = 1 INTERSECT SELECT student_id FROM enrolments WHERE course_id = 3;

title: NULLs and sets
prompt: Show the different manager_id values that aren't an employee id, using EXCEPT. NULL appears as one row, because EXCEPT treats NULLs as equal.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT manager_id FROM employees EXCEPT SELECT id FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id FROM employees EXCEPT SELECT manager_id FROM employees;
SELECT manager_id FROM employees WHERE manager_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM employees);

title: Bought Kitchen, never Home
prompt: Show the name of customers who bought a Kitchen product but never a Home product.
hints: Use EXCEPT in a subquery, then look up names.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); UPDATE order_items SET product_id = 7 WHERE order_id = 12;

solutions: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT o.customer_id FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Kitchen' EXCEPT SELECT o.customer_id FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Home');

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT o.customer_id FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Kitchen');
SELECT name FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT o.customer_id FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = i.product_id WHERE p.category = 'Home');
